text_blocks.snippet: Homeowners in Utah typically pay $9,375 to $21,000 for an asphalt shingle roof replacement and $18,000 to $35,000 for metal, with financing available through [Highlight start] contractor promotional plans, home equity options, personal loans, or homeowners insurance claims [Highlight end] .
snippet_highlighted_words: [Highlight start] contractor promotional plans, home equity options, personal loans, or homeowners insurance claims [Highlight end]

list.snippet: Asphalt shingle replacement: $10,000–$21,000 (or ~$9,375–$19,575 across general Utah estimates). On a $15,500 replacement, a 24-month 0% APR plan equals $645.83/month (12 months at 0% is $1,291.67/month), while a 10-year loan at 8% APR is about $188.06/month ($22,566.93 total paid).
Metal replacement: $18,000–$35,000, often chosen for higher snow loads, freeze-thaw durability, and high-elevation UV exposure.
Insurance deductibles: If storm, wind, or hail damage qualifies under your policy, out-of-pocket costs may be limited largely to your deductible.

Contractor financing & promotions: Many Utah roofers offer promotional financing or payment plans. Examples include Soleo Home (0% financing for 24 months), We Do Roofing Salt Lake City (12-month 0% interest option), Olympus Cove Roofing (6 months no interest and no payments), Legacy Roofing (zero-down options with 10- to 20-year terms and soft-pull pre-qualification), and RHIVE Construction (0% APR options and a 10% project savings credit promotion). You can also check 360 Roofing for $0-down, 0% APR financing on approved credit, Timberline Roofing for local financing and insurance assistance, or EZ Roofing for Utah financing and roof inspections.
Home equity loan or HELOC: Useful for larger balances or longer repayment timelines, secured by your home's equity.
Personal loan: Provides fixed monthly payments without using your home as collateral, though rates and terms depend on credit.
Insurance claim: Worth checking first if wind, hail, or winter storm damage contributed to roof wear.

Compare total cost, not just monthly payment: Promotional 0% offers can have shorter payoff windows or deferred-interest rules if not paid off on time, while longer-term loans lower monthly payments but increase total interest.
Verify credit impact and fees: Ask whether pre-qualification uses a soft pull and check for any origination or dealer fees rolled into the contract price.
Get multiple itemized quotes: Compare scope (tear-off, decking, underlayment, snow/elevation factors) across at least two or three contractors.
